summary.text: Adam Long is a Republican candidate for the South Dakota House of Representatives, District 2, in the November 3, 2026 general election, after advancing from the June 2 Republican primary.

A U.S. Navy veteran and small business owner, he is a volunteer firefighter and says he is running to push for zero-based budgeting, responsible economic growth and support for volunteer fire departments.

paragraphs.text: Adam Long served in the U.S. Navy from 2001 to 2018 and lists his profession as business owner.
In a 2026 Ballotpedia survey, Long said he returned to South Dakota to raise his family and build small businesses, and that he and his wife Stacey have four children.

He said he is a firefighter and president of the board of the Split Rock Volunteer Fire Department, a youth soccer coach in Brandon and a board member of Hope Harbor, and that he helped build the nonprofit Healing Warriors.
He also said he serves as South Dakota's Wounded Warrior Project volunteer government affairs advocate and, with his wife, as elected precinct committeeman for Precinct 4-17.

Long's three campaign messages in the survey were getting the state on a real budget through zero-based budgeting, growth that does not rely on corporate subsidies, and support for volunteer fire departments.
He said data centers and other large companies should pay the full cost of their utilities and infrastructure.
